record.original_question: For a non-orthogonal term-rewriting or combinatory reduction system R, suppose redexes can be mapped to a well-founded linear order so that residual redex degrees never increase and newly created redexes have strictly smaller degree than their creator. Does this decreasing-redexes property imply termination? If not, which useful subclasses still satisfy the implication?

evidence.quote: Is it true for non-orthogonal systems that decreasing redexes implies termination?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let R be a (possibly non-orthogonal) term-rewriting system or combinatory reduction system. A redex in a term is an occurrence of a subterm matching the left-hand side of some rule. Given a one-step reduction t →_u t' contracting a redex u, the standard residual theory associates to every other redex v in t a (possibly empty) set of residual redexes v/u in t', and identifies certain redexes in t' as new (created) redexes that are not residuals of any redex in t.

Suppose there exists a well-founded linear order (D, <) and an assignment of a "degree" d(v) ∈ D to every redex occurrence (in every reachable term), satisfying:
(i) for every redex v and every redex u, every residual v' ∈ v/u satisfies d(v') ≤ d(v); and
(ii) every redex w in t' that is created by the contraction of u in t satisfies d(w) < d(u).

Call such an assignment a decreasing-redexes labelling, and say R has the decreasing-redexes property if such a labelling exists.

Question: Does the existence of a decreasing-redexes labelling imply that R is terminating (strongly normalizing) for arbitrary, not necessarily orthogonal, term-rewriting systems and combinatory reduction systems? If not, identify natural subclasses of non-orthogonal systems for which the decreasing-redexes property does imply termination.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the decreasing-redexes condition implies termination for non-orthogonal term-rewriting and combinatory reduction systems appears in standard collections of open problems in rewriting (e.g. the RTA list of open problems) and no published resolution was found. Related work by van Oostrom on decreasing diagrams addresses confluence rather than termination, and recent literature continues to treat the non-orthogonal termination implication as unresolved. Status best classified as open.

status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems in rewriting maintained by the RTA community, including questions on decreasing labellings and termination for non-orthogonal systems.
status_evidence.claim: The problem appears in the standard rewriting open-problems list and is not marked as solved.

status_evidence.title: Confluence by Decreasing Diagrams (van Oostrom)
status_evidence.snippet: Decreasing diagrams characterize confluence in abstract rewriting; termination implications for non-orthogonal systems are not established.
status_evidence.claim: The decreasing-diagrams technique addresses confluence, not termination, leaving the termination question open.
